edit.subject: vassal_of
edit.scope: Whether a lord was in turn the vassal of his own vassal, for one feudal tie between two parties.

direct.prompt: Is the relation 'was a vassal of' symmetric?

derived.prompt: William, Duke of Normandy, was a vassal of King Philip I of France. Does it follow that King Philip I of France was a vassal of William, Duke of Normandy?
bridge: William, Duke of Normandy, was a vassal of King Philip I of France.
chain: William, Duke of Normandy, was a vassal of King Philip I of France. (given in prompt)
So King Philip I of France was a vassal of William, Duke of Normandy: yes.

derived.prompt: King John of England, as Duke of Normandy, was a vassal of King Philip II of France. Does it follow that King Philip II of France was a vassal of King John of England?
bridge: King John of England, as Duke of Normandy, was a vassal of King Philip II of France.
chain: King John of England, as Duke of Normandy, was a vassal of King Philip II of France. (given in prompt)
So King Philip II of France was a vassal of King John of England: yes.

notes: Symmetry added to a relation that is asymmetric (vassal_of is tagged asymmetric in RELATIONS.md). Both instances are the famous case of the Dukes of Normandy holding Normandy from the French king; the reverse tie never existed, so the real-world answer is clear. The delete removes the asymmetry, so its instance questions are rephrased as 'was not a vassal of', the conclusion asymmetry licensed. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
